title: Long Pressed Name
statement:
Someone meant to type the string `name`, but any key they pressed may have stuck, so each intended character could have come out one or more times in a row instead of exactly once. The text that actually appeared is `typed`.

Return `true` if `typed` could be obtained from `name` by replacing each character of `name` with one or more copies of that same character, and `false` otherwise. No character may be dropped, reordered or replaced by a different letter.
constraints: name and typed contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Every character of `typed` has only two honest explanations: it is the next character of `name` we were waiting for, or it is an extra copy of the key that was just pressed. A brute-force view splits both strings into runs of equal letters and checks that the runs line up with `typed`'s runs never shorter; walking both strings with two pointers checks the same thing in one pass without building the runs.

## Approach

1. Keep `i`, the position of the next character of `name` still to be matched.
2. Scan `typed` with `j` from left to right.
3. If `typed[j]` equals `name[i]`, it is the intended keystroke: advance `i`.
4. Otherwise it must repeat the previous typed character (`typed[j - 1]`); if it is the first character or a new letter, return `false`.
5. After the scan, every character of `name` must have been matched: return `i === name.length`.

## Example 1, step by step

`name = "alex"`, `typed = "aaleex"`.

- `j = 0`: `a` matches `name[0]`, so `i = 1`.
- `j = 1`: `a` is not `name[1] = l`, but it repeats `typed[0]`, so it is a long press.
- `j = 2`: `l` matches, `i = 2`. `j = 3`: `e` matches, `i = 3`.
- `j = 4`: `e` is not `x`, but repeats `typed[3]`, so it is skipped.
- `j = 5`: `x` matches, `i = 4`.

All four letters of `name` were matched, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): each character of `typed` is looked at once and `i` only moves forward.
- Space: O(1): two indices.

## Pitfalls

- Check `i < name.length` before reading `name[i]`; extra trailing characters must still be repeats.
- Prefer matching `name[i]` before treating a character as a repeat, so `name = "aab"` with `typed = "aab"` uses both `a`s.
- Do not return `true` just because `typed` ran out: `name = "saeed"` needs the second `e`, which is why the final `i === name.length` check matters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | index of the next character of `name` to match |
| `j` | index of the current character of `typed` |

narration.2: i points at the next character of name that still has to appear in typed.
narration.4: Walk through every character that was actually typed.
narration.5: If it is the character name expects next, it is an intended keystroke.
narration.6: Count it by moving to the next character of name.
narration.7: Otherwise it has to repeat the previous typed character; at the start or after a different letter it cannot.
narration.8: That character has no explanation, so typed cannot come from name.
narration.11: Every typed character was explained; name is reproduced only if all of its characters were matched.
